degradation kinetics in DS-S/Fe(II) are best described by a pseudo-first order rate law, and that rate constants are related to thermodynamic properties of target compounds.

the degradation kinetics of chlorinated organic compounds by Fe(II)/cement slurries can be correlated to the thermodynamic properties of the compounds.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
degradation kinetics of chlorinated hydrocarbons by ferrous iron in cement slurries are affected by the chemical properties of the chlorinated compounds.
the rate of degradation by Fe(II)/Fe(III) is affected by a variety of factors including Fe(II)/ Fe(III) ratio, pH, target organic concentration and target organic properties such as E(LUMO).
the rate of dechlorination of chlorinated alkanes and chlorinated ethenes is controlled by both thermodynamics and kinetics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the rate of degradation of chlorinated alkanes is faster than chlorinated ethyenes in DS/S- Fe(II) systems and that the rate constant for degradation of chlorinated ethenes increases with increasing E(LUMO).

degradation of chlorinated alkanes and alkenes by Fe(II), in the presence of cement, was faster when the lowest unoccupied molecular orbitals of the chlorinated organic compound had lower energy levels.

degradation kinetics in DS/Fe(II) is dependent on thermodynamic parameters such as E(LUMO), which can provide an effective tool for the prediction of degradation rates for chlorinated aliphatics in DS/Fe systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the degradation kinetics of chlorinated hydrocarbons by DS/S-Fe (II) are affected by the molecular structure of the target organic compounds.
the degradation kinetics of chlorinated organic compounds by Fe(II)-activated cement slurries can be predicted by the LUMO energies.
the degradation of chlorinated alkanes by Fe(II)-cement slurries is a thermodynamically favorable reaction and the rate constant is dependent on the E(LUMO) of the chlorinated aliphatics.
